subject: Affine Memory_budget transfer through ordinary WVB 1.33 calls
claim: The Windows source-built compiler and scalar runner transfer an entry or split child Memory_budget by value through one ordinary direct call, preserve the child's exact limit, reject duplicate transfer, and report exact budget exhaustion.

runs.target: Source-built emitter and WVB 1.33 scalar runner
runs.command: Build the emission driver and WVB runner from their current project manifests with the pinned local split-compiler producers, then package each with the development cache.

runs.target: Compiler, verifier, affine budget, and scalar unsafe-scratch boundary
runs.summary: source-wir-cases=11 valid=2 rejected=9 malformed-wir=9 malformed-wvb=7 semantic-wvb=3 compiler-verifier-cases=11 runtime-cases=6 runtime-malformed=1 result=42 allocation=zeroed teardown=bounded

limitations: The claim covers by-value direct calls only. An ordinary immutable Memory_budget borrow remains valid through source and WIR but WVB emission returns Unsupported_shape because WVB 1.33 has no borrowed-budget call encoding.
The bounded scalar provider still limits scratch length to 64 bytes and alignment to 8, exposes no pointer or host address, and keeps backing and lease state interpreter-private.
The focused run forces child-budget exhaustion but does not force bounded-heap refusal.
Native lowering, pointer and write-region operations, authenticated Foreign calls, a migrated real boundary, and published-front-door reconstruction remain pending.
The run is local Windows development evidence and does not claim Linux reproduction, paired-host conformance, qualification, release, or independent reproduction.

The focused oracle was used instead of the eight-owner changed-file development plan because the broad plan would repeat Seed, lowerer, containment, callable, and memory suites beyond the changed behavior.
